- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices drop sharply, model often underestimates the fall; increase downward adjustment or add volatility buffer.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged upward trend; cap forecast growth after spike.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after rising), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with recent 5–7 day moving average.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong downward momentum, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment shifts.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges the cycle’s direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from model, check if sentiment was neutral or bearish; if so, apply a 3–5 day lag correction to avoid overconfidence in short-term trends.
